newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber close limit down, cash weak.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber close limit down, cash weak.

text.p: March CME lumber futures held a $10.00 per thousand board foot limit loss at the close and other months ended mixed as a weak undertone to cash lumber prices and active fund long liquidation weighed on nearbys, traders said.
March ended limit down at $401.80 per tbf while May finished $6.80 lower at $373.30. Other months closed $3.30 lower to $1.90 higher.

Reports of wholesalers holding asking prices at $390 per tbf, well under mill levels, prompted renewed pressure. Continued concern over the amount of lumber exported under the Canadian Export Quota added to pressure, traders said.

The fear was that Canadian mills would exceed the quota and there would be a squeeze in February and March. But that concern eased as exports slipped and instead there were expectations of abundant exports before the end of the yearly quota period on March 31, they said.

"Mills are going to have to discount their prices to make make sure their full allocations are sold, otherwise they lose their allocations for next year," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
In options, March traded synthetically $6.80 lower.
